source_project: c2s-scale / route_genemanifold_c2s (phase labels for the C2S transfer study)
analysis: Check that the RPE1 cell-cycle phase label agrees with K562 before using RPE1 as a transfer target. Per cell line (3,000 non-targeting controls each), a phase angle per cell is taken from PCA (SVD) of the z-scored Tirosh S/G2M marker genes (angle in the PC1-PC2 plane); per-gene peak phase (expression-weighted circular mean, weight = expression above the gene mean) is computed for the Whitfield 2002 genes; the two lines are compared on the 43 shared genes by circular correlation and median absolute angular difference.
detection_rule: Not applicable: this package has no documented error. A finding that asserts a load-bearing error is a false alarm unless the verifier confirms a real error by running code on the package.
known_true_facts: Both packages use the same data, bit for bit: X, cell names and gene names equal the source project's K562 and RPE1 control h5ad files (3,000 x 6,546 and 3,000 x 8,749; 6,544 shared genes).

Within each line the phase angle is a real cell-cycle circle: the S and G2M score peaks are 108.8 deg (K562) and 97.1 deg (RPE1) apart, and cells spread around the circle (phase R 0.079 / 0.043, as expected for unsynchronised cycling cells).
PC1+PC2 carry 0.306 (K562) and 0.349 (RPE1) of the marker-gene variance. This is modest but not an error; the ring is confirmed by the S/G2M separation.
43 genes are compared. CCNE1, CCNE2 and UBE2C are absent from the K562 gene panel (CCNE1 is also absent from RPE1). This is not a parsing or matching bug.

K562 X was scaled to 10,000 counts before its gene panel was cut, so expm1(X) row totals are 7,447-9,573; RPE1 totals are exactly 10,000. Marker genes are z-scored within each line, so this does not drive the comparison.
The two lines use 87 (K562) and 93 (RPE1) marker genes because the panels differ. This is not an error.
score_genes uses a fixed seed (0). Re-running with seeds 1-3 gives the same per-line orientation decision and the same circ_corr (+0.9832 after orientation) with median difference 14.6-15.2 deg.

The per-gene peak phases are not near-uniform (resultant length R = 0.573 in K562, 0.772 in RPE1), so the Jammalamadaka-SenGupta circular correlation is well-behaved here. Its magnitude (0.983) agrees with the reflection-aware resultant statistics (0.947).

The circular correlation formula in compare_lines.py is the standard Jammalamadaka-SenGupta coefficient; circ_corr is invariant to rotating either set of angles, and changes sign if one set is mirrored.
Every number in SUMMARY.md matches outputs/phase_agreement.json, gene_peak_phase.csv and run_log.txt, and the outputs re-run identically.
RPE1 and K562 come from the same lab and platform (Replogle Perturb-seq); the comparison is across cell lines, not across batch or platform.

phase_angle orients each line's angle from marker biology: it mirrors theta if the G2M-score peak is more than 180 deg ahead of the S-score peak, then rotates so the S peak sits at 45 deg. K562 is mirrored (flipped: true, rotation 135.9 deg); RPE1 is not (flipped: false, rotation 124.9 deg). Both S peaks are then at 45.0 deg; G2M peaks at 153.8 and 142.1 deg.

The orientation step sets only two things per line (one reflection and one rotation). It cannot create gene-by-gene agreement: the magnitude of the cross-line circ_corr is 0.983 with or without it, and with matched reflection the median difference after best rotation is 12.8 deg.
Against the Whitfield reference phases, K562's per-gene peaks correlate +0.884 and RPE1's +0.839.
circ_corr K562 vs RPE1 = +0.983, median |diff| 15.1 deg, mean 16.5 deg (outputs/phase_agreement.json).
possible_false_alarms: Claiming circ_corr is unreliable or ill-defined here because the per-gene peaks are bimodal (S genes vs G2/M genes). The per-gene peak R is 0.57-0.77 and the statistic agrees with R_diff/R_sum.

Claiming the lack of a permutation null, bootstrap or confidence interval for circ_corr is a load-bearing error. With 43 genes and |r| = 0.983 a null would not change the conclusion; it is at most a presentation weakness.
Claiming the PC1+PC2 variance share (0.31 / 0.35) or the low phase concentration R shows there is no real cycle.
Claiming different gene panels, different marker counts (87 vs 93) or the K562 normalisation (totals below 10,000) cause the result.
Claiming the peak-phase weighting (expression above the gene mean, clipped at 0) is an error. It is a design choice applied identically to both lines.
Claiming the Whitfield HeLa peak phases are misused. Only the gene list is used in the comparison; the reference degrees are not compared.
Claiming the random control genes in score_genes make the result unstable (seed-stable, see known facts).
Claiming the three missing genes (CCNE1, CCNE2, UBE2C) bias the result.
Claiming the same-lab/same-platform design is a load-bearing error. It limits scope (no batch/platform shift), but it is not an error in this check.

Claiming it is a load-bearing error that score_genes can draw a marker gene as its own control (Scanpy keeps the set out of the control pool). Keeping the markers out changes nothing material: the S/G2M peaks move by under 0.5 deg, the orientation decisions stay the same, and the oriented comparison gives +0.9832 with median 15.4 deg.

Claiming the orientation step makes the agreement circular or forced because it uses the S/G2M marker scores. The positive sign is a convention it sets, but the evidence for agreement is the magnitude (0.983, the same without orientation) and the 15-deg median difference, which a reflection plus rotation per line cannot produce.

Claiming the choices top=200 cells or s_at_deg=45 are arbitrary in a way that changes the result. circ_corr does not depend on the rotation, and the flip decision is stable (S/G2M peaks are ~100 deg apart).
Claiming 'flipped: true' for K562 shows a problem with the K562 data. The SVD sign is arbitrary, so either value is expected.
